## Fire Protection Engineering Services in Florida

A Florida-licensed Professional Engineer prepares or reviews every deliverable. You get sealed, permit-ready documents for projects across Central Florida and statewide.

You have drawings. You need a Florida PE seal.

### Plan Review & PE Stamping

PE Seal · NFPA 13 / 72

You made the drawings. We review them, fix code issues, and seal them. Your submittal gets the PE certification the AHJ requires.

Best for: Design-build sprinkler and alarm contractors, and MEP firms without a fire protection engineer on staff.

#### Third-Party Plan Review

Independent review of sprinkler and fire alarm drawings against NFPA 13, NFPA 72, and the FBC.

#### PE Sealing of Contractor Drawings

Once the package is compliant, we sign and seal it for permit.

We answer plan review comments and revise the drawings until the comments are closed.

PE Seal · Florida

## Plan Review & PE Stamping in Florida

EverSafe Fire Protection provides independent third-party plan review and PE sealing of fire sprinkler and fire alarm drawings for contractors and MEP firms. When your drawings need a Florida-licensed engineer's stamp to clear permitting, we review, correct, and seal them.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Independent review of sprinkler and fire alarm drawings for NFPA 13 / NFPA 72 and Florida Building Code compliance

- Marked-up comments and coordination with your design team

- PE sealing of compliant drawing packages

- Support responding to AHJ plan review comments

- Fast turnaround for permit-driven schedules

Why It Matters

### Why PE-stamped matters

Many contractors prepare quality drawings in-house but cannot legally seal them — only a Florida-licensed professional engineer can. Third-party PE stamping gives your submittal the engineering certification the AHJ requires, without the cost of a full engineering department. Our review looks for code issues before the drawings go to the AHJ.

NFPA 13 · Florida

## Fire Sprinkler System Design in Florida

EverSafe Fire Protection provides fire sprinkler system design for commercial, industrial, and mission-critical buildings across Florida. Our designs are prepared by a Florida-licensed fire protection engineer and delivered PE-stamped and permit-ready.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Wet, dry, pre-action, and antifreeze system layout and design

- Hydraulic calculations and water supply analysis

- Riser and equipment details coordinated with architectural and MEP plans

- Design in accordance with NFPA 13 and the Florida Building Code

- PE-stamped, permit-ready drawing packages

Why It Matters

### Why PE-stamped matters

Most Florida jurisdictions require fire sprinkler drawings to bear the seal of a licensed professional engineer before a permit is issued. PE-stamped fire protection drawings clear plan review faster because the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) can rely on the engineer's certification of code compliance. Our permit-ready packages reduce review cycles and keep your project schedule on track.

NFPA 13 · IFC Ch. 32 · Florida

## High-Piled Storage Fire Protection Design in Florida

Warehouses and distribution centers live or die on their storage configuration. EverSafe evaluates your commodity classification, storage heights, and rack arrangements, then sets the sprinkler design criteria — density, ESFR, or in-rack — per NFPA 13 and IFC Chapter 32, so the design protects the actual hazard instead of the assumed one.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Commodity classification and storage arrangement review

- Sprinkler design criteria: ESFR, density/area, or in-rack protection

- Flue space, clearance, and aisle-width compliance checks

- Smoke and heat vent / draft curtain coordination

- High-piled storage permit plan support

- Design criteria for racking changes and expansions

Why It Matters

### Why storage design is a specialty

High-piled storage is where generic sprinkler designs fail — the wrong commodity class or a missed in-rack requirement shows up as an AHJ rejection or, worse, an unprotected rack. Engineer-set criteria before the shop drawings start keeps the project, and the building, protected.

NFPA 101 · 101A · FBC · Florida

## Life Safety & Egress in Florida

EverSafe Fire Protection prepares life safety plan sheets and egress analysis for AHJ review. Our Florida-licensed fire protection engineer documents occupancy, egress, and compartmentation per the Florida Building Code and NFPA 101.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Occupancy classification and occupant load calculations

- Egress paths, exits, and exit-discharge documentation

- Fire and smoke barrier / compartmentation plans

- Travel distance, common-path, and dead-end analysis

- Areas of refuge and accessible egress coordination

- Coordination with the architect’s permit plan set

- Fire Safety Evaluation System (FSES) worksheets per NFPA 101A for existing buildings

Why It Matters

### Why life safety plans hold up permits

Most AHJ plan-review comments trace back to incomplete life safety documentation — missing occupant loads, unproven travel distances, or barrier ratings that don’t match the occupancy. A sealed life safety analysis answers those questions before the reviewer asks them, cutting a review cycle out of your permit timeline.

IFC Ch. 50 · FBC · Florida

## Hazardous Materials Inventory Statements (HMIS) in Florida

When your project stores or uses hazardous materials, the AHJ wants an inventory statement before the permit moves. EverSafe prepares HMIS documentation listing material classifications, quantities, and storage/use locations per the Florida Building Code and IFC Chapter 50 — the deliverable hazmat permits are built on.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Hazardous material classification per IFC

- Quantity tabulation by storage and use, per control area

- Storage vs. in-use quantities and conditions of use

- Location plans tied to your floor layouts

- Coordination with MAQ analysis and hazmat permit applications

Why It Matters

### Why the inventory statement matters

The HMIS is the AHJ’s first read on your hazmat risk. A complete, engineer-prepared statement shortens hazmat permit review and gives your MAQ analysis and permit application a defensible technical basis.

---
Source: https://eversafe-fire.com/maq-analysis-florida.html

IFC 5003 · FBC · Florida

## Maximum Allowable Quantity (MAQ) Analysis in Florida

Exceed the maximum allowable quantity in a control area and the occupancy classification changes — with it, the construction type, fire protection, and permit path. EverSafe runs the MAQ analysis per IFC Table 5003.1.1, accounting for sprinkler and storage-cabinet increases, so you know exactly where your project stands before the AHJ decides for you.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Control-area quantity analysis against MAQ tables

- Sprinkler and approved storage-cabinet quantity increases

- Storage vs. use and open vs. closed system breakdowns

- H-occupancy determination support

- Recommendations: subdivide control areas or reduce quantities

- Sealed report for AHJ and permit submittal

Why It Matters

### Why MAQ analysis decides the project

MAQ is the hinge between a standard occupancy and a high-hazard one. Getting it right early tells you whether the design needs another control area, a different occupancy, or nothing at all — a decision worth making on paper, not in plan review.

---
Source: https://eversafe-fire.com/fire-smoke-modeling-florida.html

FDS / CFD · Florida

## Fire & Smoke Modeling (FDS/CFD) in Florida

EverSafe Fire Protection provides performance-based fire and smoke modeling using Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) tool. We serve architects, engineers, and building owners across Florida on projects where prescriptive code solutions don't fit.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- FDS/CFD modeling of fire growth, smoke movement, and tenability

- Smoke control system analysis and verification

- Tenability studies for egress and occupant safety

- Performance-based design documentation for AHJ submittal

- Coordination with the design team and the AHJ on acceptance criteria

Why It Matters

### Why PE-stamped matters

Performance-based designs ask the AHJ to accept an engineered solution in place of a prescriptive one. A Florida-licensed fire protection engineer's seal on the modeling report signals that the analysis follows accepted engineering practice.

---
Source: https://eversafe-fire.com/smoke-studies-florida.html

NFPA 92 · FBC · Florida

## Smoke Control Studies & Smoke Management in Florida

Atriums, malls, high-rises, and underground spaces need engineered proof that smoke stays manageable. EverSafe performs smoke control studies — rational analysis, pressurization design, and exhaust sizing per NFPA 92 — and backs them with CFD modeling when the AHJ wants to see the smoke move.

Last updated: November 10, 2026

What's Included

### What's included

- Smoke control rational analysis per NFPA 92

- Stairwell and elevator hoistway pressurization design

- Atrium and large-volume smoke exhaust studies

- Tenability and smoke-layer analysis

- Coordination with mechanical design and commissioning

- CFD-backed studies via our fire & smoke modeling service

Why It Matters

### Why smoke studies need an engineer

Smoke control is performance-based by nature — the AHJ approves the analysis, not just the equipment. A sealed rational analysis with modeled tenability gives reviewers the engineering basis they are looking for.

FAQs · Florida

## Fire Protection Engineering FAQs

Straight answers to the questions Florida contractors, MEP firms, architects, and building owners ask us about fire protection engineering, permitting, and PE-stamped deliverables.

#### Who can stamp fire sprinkler drawings in Florida?

Only a professional engineer licensed in the State of Florida can sign and seal fire sprinkler drawings submitted for permit. Most Florida jurisdictions require the PE seal on sprinkler and fire alarm plans before they will issue a permit. EverSafe Fire Protection is a Florida-licensed fire protection engineering practice, and all of our drawing packages are PE-stamped and permit-ready.

#### What does a fire protection engineer do?

A fire protection engineer designs the systems that detect, suppress, and control fire in buildings — primarily fire sprinkler and fire alarm systems. The work includes system layout, hydraulic and electrical calculations, code compliance analysis, and sealing drawings for permit. Fire protection engineers also perform code consulting, risk analysis, and performance-based design such as fire and smoke modeling.

#### How much does fire sprinkler system design cost?

Design fees depend on building size, system complexity, and how complete the architectural and MEP backgrounds are. EverSafe works on a fixed-fee basis, so you know the price before we start. Send us your project details through our proposal form and we will respond with a fixed-fee quote — typical turnaround is 1 day.

#### How long does fire alarm design take?

It depends on the size and complexity of the building and the quality of the background drawings provided. Straightforward commercial projects move quickly; large or phased projects take longer. We give you a schedule with every fixed-fee proposal, and we prioritize permit-driven deadlines.

#### What do you need from me to prepare a proposal?

A brief description of the project is enough to start: building type and size, location in Florida, which services you need (sprinkler design, alarm design, stamping, consulting), and your permit timeline. If you have architectural backgrounds or plans, attach them — but they are not required for an initial quote.

#### Do you serve clients outside Central Florida?

Yes. We are based in Central Florida and serve clients statewide, including the Orlando, Tampa, Miami, and Jacksonville markets. All coordination can be handled remotely, and our PE-stamped deliverables are accepted by AHJs throughout Florida.

#### What is a third-party plan review?

A third-party plan review is an independent engineering review of fire protection drawings prepared by someone else — typically a contractor or MEP firm. We check the drawings against NFPA 13, NFPA 72, and the Florida Building Code, mark up any issues, and then PE-seal the compliant package so it can be submitted for permit.

#### What codes do you design to?

We design to the Florida Building Code and the NFPA standards it references, including NFPA 13 (sprinkler systems), NFPA 72 (fire alarm systems), NFPA 101 (life safety), NFPA 80 (fire doors), NFPA 92 (smoke control), and NFPA 855 (energy storage systems), as applicable to each project.

#### What is fire and smoke modeling used for?

Fire and smoke modeling uses computational fluid dynamics (FDS/CFD) software to simulate how fire and smoke behave in a building. It is used for performance-based designs where prescriptive code doesn't fit — such as atria, large open spaces, and complex smoke control systems — and to demonstrate to the AHJ that occupants can safely egress.

#### Do you design for energy storage systems and data centers?

Yes. We provide fire protection design for mission-critical facilities including data centers and energy storage systems, designed in accordance with NFPA 855 where applicable. This includes hazard analysis, suppression system selection, and clean agent system design, all PE-stamped and permit-ready.

#### What happens if the AHJ rejects the drawings?

Our process includes permit support. If the AHJ sends comments, we answer them and revise the drawings.

#### How fast can I get a proposal?

Our typical fixed-fee proposal turnaround is 1 day. Submit the Request a Proposal form with your project details, or call 386-837-4057 / email info@eversafe-fire.com, and we will respond with a fixed-fee quote and schedule.

#### How do I upload my drawings?

Use the instant quote for PE review and seal. After the price shows, an upload area appears on the same page. Add your drawings and calcs, then press Request this job. Upload is optional.

#### What files do you need for a PE review?

Your drawings and calculations. We accept PDF, DWG, DXF, RVT, ZIP, JPG, and PNG files. Each file can be up to 100 MB, with up to 20 files and 500 MB per quote.

#### Is my drawing set kept private?

Yes. Uploaded files are stored privately and are not public. Only EverSafe can open them. Files are deleted from the website server after 90 days.

#### Do you work outside Florida?

No. We work on Florida projects only. We are based in Central Florida and serve all of Florida.

#### What is your Florida registry number?

FBPE Registry No. 40449. EverSafe Fire Protection is a registered Florida engineering firm.
